newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada ahead on budget, economy strong - Martin.
newsitem.headline: Canada ahead on budget, economy strong - Martin.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Monday the budget he will present on Feb. 18 will be in the context of a strong economy that is delivering better-than-expected results in the deficit reduction battle.
"We're bringing the budget down against a background of very good news. Most economists are projecting very strong job creation this year and next," Martin told reporters.

"It's quite clear that Canada will have one of the strongest growth records of any of the G7 (Group of Seven) countries. We're doing very well on the deficit. All in all, it's very clear that we are well into the recovery."
Martin, who has in the past rejected calls from the Conservative and Reform parties for broad tax cuts, said there could be "very targeted" tax cuts.
"In very targeted areas, we envisage the possibility even of tax cuts," he said in French.

Asked whether Canadians could expect the equivalent of a "peace dividend" to compensate for his deficit-cutting in the past few years, he said the government would try to operate on parallel tracks in this regard -- continuing deficit cuts while investing in the future.

"Canadians essentially do not want us to spend the 'dividend' before it's been earned. They know that we still have a very large deficit. We have done very well. We're well ahead of our targets. But Canadians effectively want us to deal with the deficit, and that we intend to do," he said.

"At the same time, it has always been our intention to build for the future. We demonstrated this in last year's budget -- the working income supplement for children, the technology partnerships program. And we will continue to operate really on both tracks, that is to say, deficit reduction, economic growth and jobs."

"The chief economist of the Bank of Montreal today announced that he was expecting the creation of more than 700,000 new jobs in the next two years," Martin said in French. "I am very optimistic in regard to the future."

The finance minister declined to speculate whether his announcing the budget was another signal that a general election could be held early. Many analysts expect a June election, arguing the government is clearing its calendar, while others mention September or October. An election does not have to be called until late 1998.
